name: Shami Kabab
description: Classic Pakistani shami kababs made from tender beef and chana dal cooked until dry, ground with spices and herbs, then shallow-fried.
ingredients: 1 cup chana dal, rinsed and soaked for 30 minutes
½ cup fresh coriander and mint, chopped
method: Put beef, soaked chana dal, onion, ginger-garlic paste, whole spices and salt in a pot. Add enough water to cook the mixture without leaving excess liquid.
Cover and simmer until the beef and dal are completely tender. Uncover near the end and cook, stirring, until the mixture is dry; excess moisture can make the kababs break.
Cool slightly, remove any large hard spice pieces if desired, then grind to a smooth but firm mixture.
Mix in green chilies, coriander, mint and enough beaten egg to bind; do not add more egg than needed.
Shape into flat patties. Chill for 15–20 minutes if the mixture feels soft.
Heat a thin layer of oil over medium heat and shallow-fry the kababs until golden on both sides and hot throughout.
Drain briefly and serve with chutney, onion and lemon.
tips: The cooked beef-and-dal mixture must be quite dry before grinding.
Add egg gradually; too much liquid can make shami kababs fragile.
storage: Cool promptly and refrigerate cooked kababs for up to 2 days. Unfried shaped kababs can also be frozen in a single layer, then packed once firm.
